findings.claim: Round one. file_facts() computed named_in_solution with an exact comparison, feeding Jev's reviewer_must_read state with a false 'not named' for every file under a directory the plan names.
findings.failure_scenario: A solution plan names a directory, as SEEN-114's formatter slices named apps and packages. Every file under it was reported to Jev as not named by the solution record, defeating the purpose of the ticket at the one place the wrong answer does the most harm.
findings.resolution: harness/triage.py:522 now reads named_in_solution=covers(path, named), with covers imported from harness/paths.py. The third round traced the whole call chain from file_facts to file_subject, confirmed no other hand-written comparison remains in it, and reran NoSecondReaderTest against the tree to find zero offenders. RED record 36, GREEN record 37.
findings.rule_candidate: none: rules/registry.toml does not exist on this branch, because SEEN-114 creates it and has not landed.

findings.claim: Round two. The instrument scanned a hardcoded four-module allowlist, so a reader of the question born in any unlisted module would pass it silently.
findings.failure_scenario: A future ticket adds harness/scoring.py reimplementing the membership test; the allowlist never looks at it and the regression test stays green while a fifth reader exists, reproducing the defect this ticket exists to prevent.
findings.resolution: The allowlist is removed and the scan is every harness/*.py unconditionally, which was only possible once kpi.py's local named, holding agent names, became agent_names. The third round checked the rename is complete across harness/*.py and test_kpi.py and found no leftover reader. RED record 45, GREEN record 46.
findings.rule_candidate: none: rules/registry.toml does not exist on this branch, because SEEN-114 creates it and has not landed.

findings.claim: Round two. The comparator was matched against its unparsed text, so a comparison against the same set wrapped in a fallback was not recognised.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit in triage.py writes `if path in (entry.get('files') or []):` instead of calling covers. The exact text match does not see it and a hand-written reader reappears undetected.
findings.resolution: The comparator is matched structurally, and after F4 it is matched as what the comparator is rather than what it contains: the plan's file list, or an or whose alternatives include it. test_a_comparator_wrapped_in_a_fallback_is_seen reproduces the pattern and the third round ran it independently. RED record 45, GREEN records 46 and 54.
findings.rule_candidate: none: rules/registry.toml does not exist on this branch, because SEEN-114 creates it and has not landed.

findings.claim: Round three, raised against the fix that round had just confirmed. Walking every node of a comparator flagged any bare occurrence of named or planned inside a membership test, with no requirement that the comparator be the plan's file list, and this package reuses both words for the unmet criteria of a return and the points a sprint planned.
findings.failure_scenario: A harness module writes `if cost in (planned, actual_prior):` where planned means points planned for a sprint. The instrument flags it as a second reader of the plan-coverage question, which the round reproduced by running _comparisons against that source, and a future unrelated change fails the whole regression suite on a line that never asks whether a slice's plan covers a path.
findings.resolution: _names_a_plan now asks what the comparator is: the plan's file list, or an or whose alternatives include it, which is the only wrapping that leaves it still being the list. A tuple of two unrelated things is not. RED record 53, which failed on exactly the source the round constructed, GREEN record 54, and the same test holds both shapes that are the question so the repair cannot quietly undo F2 and F3. The round's own suggestion, renaming the colliding identifiers, is right in principle and is a rename across half a dozen modules that this ticket does not own; the narrower repair is recorded in the Outcome, as is the fact that this is the one change here no independent context has read.
